The petitioner has filed this petition being aggrieved by the arbitral award passed by the Special Deputy Commissioner/Arbitrator, Bengaluru Urban District, Bengaluru, in No. LAQ / ARB /
NH-844/ CR / 43 / 2021-22 and LAQ / ARB / NH-844/ CR / 42 / 2021-22 dated 26.02.2024 pertaining to Survey No.73/2 measuring 1620 Square Meters and Survey No. A.P. No.32/2024 73/3 measuring 655 Square Meters of Halehalli village, Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru Urban District.
.2.

The definite case of the petitioner is that the property of respondent No.1 measuring 1620 Square Meters in Survey No.73/2 and 655 Square Meters in Survey No.73/3 of Halehalli village, Anekal Taluk had been acquired under Preliminary Notification dated 24.01.2019 and Final Notification dated 23.01.2020.

The respondent No.3 had passed the award and awarded a total compensation amount of Rs.27,49,844/- in respect of 1620 Square Meters and Rs. 11,02,430/- in respect of 655 Square Meters, which has been received by the respondent No.1 under protest.
Subsequently, on 13.08.2021 the respondent No.1 has filed the application for enhancing the compensation at the rate of Rs.5,00,00,000/- per acre.
Accordingly, the application is taken by the respondent No.2 for consideration.

Thereafter, the Arbitrator held an inquiry and passed common order in LAQ /
ARB / NH-844 / CR / 43/42/2021-22 dated 26.02.2024 .4.

Being aggrieved by the impugned Arbitral Award, the petitioner filed this petition under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, setting aside the following:
:GROUNDS:
The petitioner claims that the impugned is perverse, patently illegal, capricious and goes against the very fundamentals of Arbitration and Conciliation Act.

Further the respondent No.2 directly in the operative portion at page No.6 has redetermined the market value at Rs.915.93 per Square Meters i.e., Rs. 610.51 + Rs. 305/- (50% of Rs.610.51) + Rs. 92/- (Rs.610.52 - Rs.518.93).

The respondent No.2 on the basis of the aforesaid instructions has awarded 50%
addition of the guidance value of Rs.610.51 per Square Meters which has fixed for dry lands by respondent No.3 and arrived at Rs. 305/- and thereafter awarded the difference amount of Rs. 92/-
along with statutory benefits under RFCTLARR Act.

The respondent No.2 without giving any findings on the determination of market value by the respondent No.3 has observed in the operative portion of the impugned Arbitral Award at page No.6 that the respondent No.1 has contended that the respondent No.3 has fixed different market value for dry lands as some of them have ben awarded Rs.610.51 per Sq. Meters while others have received compensation @ Rs. 518.93 per Square Meters which is discriminatory on account of which the respondent No.1 is entitled to the difference amount of Rs. 92/- per Square Meters along with 50% addition on the market value since the subject lands are acquired for A.P. No.32/2024 national highways and thus the respondent No.2 has dealt with a matter which was beyond the submission to the arbitration and clearly coming within the purview of Section 34(2)(iv) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act.

The respondent No.2 makes an attempt to give sanctity to the special instructions under the notification and at the same time, conveniently disregards the classification of lands under the very same notification by awarding the difference amount to suit the needs of the respondent No.1.
The respondent No. 2 for redetermining the compensation awarded by the respondent No.3 was not in accordance with the said notification on which the reliance was placed upon for enhancement.

The impugned Arbitral Award on the face of it opposed to most basic notions of law, morality and justice since the respondent No.2 has determined the market value of the subject lands giving benefit of the law, A.P.
No.32/2024 which is not applicable for determination of the market value of the subject lands.
There is no finding in the entire impugned Arbitral Award about the category.
The respondent No.2 has also failed to follow the procedure laid down in Section 24 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act.

The very basis for passing the impugned Arbitral Award is the specific instructions but the same have no applicability to the present case on hand and the respondent No.2 ought to have examined the same before placing any reliance in a hurried manner.

The respondent No.2 has neither complied with the procedure provided under Section 24 nor decided the dispute in accordance with Section 28(1)(a) and at the same time has failed to comply with Secti8on 31(3) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act.

The impugned common Arbitral Award was passed on 26.02.2024, certified copy of the Arbitral Award was received by the petitioner on 12.03.2024 and the A.P. No.32/2024 stipulated period of 3 months commences from 12.03.2024
the petition is filed within 3 months from the date of receipt of the impugned Arbitral Award by the petitioner.
Among other grounds, prayed for relief claimed in the petition.

Point:
Before proceeding further in this case, it is relevant to note admitted and undisputed facts in this case.

The respondent No.1 Sri. Devaraju is an owner of the property bearing Survey No.73/2 measuring 1620 Sq. Meters and Survey No.73/3 measuring 655 Square Meters of Halehalli village and the said property has been acquired for widening of NH-844 under Preliminary Notification dated 24.01.2019 and Final Notification dated 23.01.2020, is an admitted fact.

It is also admitted and undisputed fact that a sum of Rs.27,49,844/- in respect of 1620 Square Meters and A.P. No.32/2024 Rs. 11,02,430/- in respect of 655 Square Meters was disbursed to the respondent No. 1 as compensation.

.10. In the case on hand, the LAO/ respondent No.3 passed the award under New Act i.e., Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

The said enhancement is under challenge in this petition with the claim of the petitioner that the LAO has passed the award by following due procedures as contemplated under Sections 26 to 30 along with first schedule of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 and claims that there is no scope for the Arbitrator to enhance the A.P. Arbitrator / respondent No.2 ought to have confirmed the award passed by the respondent No.3/ LAO.
.11.

In view of the aforesaid definite contention, it is just and necessary to see what are the criteria to determine the market value of the acquired land as per new Act has to be considered by this Court.

Section 26 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 speaks about determination of market value of the land by the Collector, Section 27 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 speaks about determination of amount of compensation,
Section 28 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 speaks about parameter considered by the Collector in determination of the award and Section 29 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 A.P. No.32/2024 speaks about determination of value of the things attached to the land or building.
Section 30 of Land Acquisition Act speaks about award of solatium.

In the context of this case, it is just and relevant to note Sections 26 and 28 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, that reads as under:
"26. Determination of market value of land by Collector- (1) The Collector shall adopt the following criteria in assessing and determining the market value of the land,
namely:--
(a) the minimum land value, if any, specified in the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 for the registration of sale deeds or agreements to sell, as the case may be, in the area, where the land is situated; or (b) the average sale price for similar type of land situated in the nearest village or nearest vicinity area; or (c) consented amount of compensation as agreed upon under sub-section (2) of section 2 in case of acquisition of lands for private companies or for public private partnership projects, whichever is higher:
Provided that the date for determination of market value shall be the date on which the notification has been issued under section 11".

sentences.text: The first schedule to the Act is in accordance with Section 30(2) of the New Act which shows that the Collector shall issue individual awards detailing the particulars of compensation payable and the details of payment of the compensation as specified in the first schedule.

In view of the aforesaid law and facts, whenever there is an application for enhancement of compensation before the Arbitrator is filed then it is the duty of the Arbitrator to see that whether the LAO followed Sections 26 to 30 of the New Act along with first schedule to the Act.
If at all the award has been passed in-consonance with the aforesaid provisions of law/new Act, certainly the Arbitrator cannot intervene with the award passed by the LAO.

Therefore, in the case on hand, it is for the petitioner to prove that the award passed by the LAO / respondent No.3 is in- A.P. No.32/2024 consonance with the aforesaid provisions of law and the respondent No.1 has to prove that the award passed by the LAO / respondent No.3 is not in consonance with the aforesaid provision of law.
As such, he has filed the petition before the Arbitrator / respondent No.2 and the respondent No.2 by considering all those facts enhanced the compensation.

.12. The definite grievance of the petitioner in this case is that the arbitrator applied 1.5 multiplier though the said multiplication is applicable to the land to the extent of only 5 guntas and the said multiplication is not applicable to this case as the extent of property is more than 5 guntas.

The petitioner also claimed that the Arbitrator has added 50% to the market value holding that acquired land is abutting to National Highway but the claim of the petitioner is that it is the newly formed highway on the acquired land and the land of the petitioner is acquired for formation of highway, as such, there is no possibility of abutting highway to the property of respondent No. 1.

Hence A.P.
No.32/2024 question of adding 50% of the market value of the property of the petitioner does not arise.
The contention raised by the petitioner is that the market value was determined, hence special instructions for enhancement of compensation is not applicable to the property of the petitioner.

sentences.text: Per contra, the respondent No. 1 has to prove that his property was abutting to the national highway prior to the acquisition of property and he is entitled for enhancement as per the special instructions as the competent authority have not declared the market value of the acquired property.
.13. As per the Gazette notification dated 05.12.2018, 1.5 multiplication is applicable only to the property that will not exceed more than 5 guntas.
The property involved in this case is almost 6 guntas and 16 A.P. No.32/2024 guntas, hence the said multiplication certainly not applicable to the present case on hand.

.14. The petitioner claims that the land involved in this case is acquired for new project and there was no existing highway so that the Arbitrator can add additional 50% of compensation but there is no material such as sketch that shows the identification of property in which the project stated in the petition had been carried out.
Hence the said contention of the petitioner cannot be accepted in this case.
.15. The petitioner during the course of arguments has produced the gazette notification dated 05.12.2018 regarding the fixing of market value / guidance value.

As per the said document, the property involved in this case i.e., property in Sy.No. 73/2 and 73/3 of Halehalli village comes under the potential Zone for which value is fixed at Rs. 14 lakhs per acre.
As per condition No. 4, in the guidance value the 50% or respective enhancement of 35, 30 or 25 percent can be added if the guidance value is not fixed.
When the A.P. No.32/2024 guidance value is fixed, question of adding aforesaid percentages certainly does not arise.
.16. I have closely perused the award passed by the Arbitrator / respondent No.2.

The Arbitrator till the 1st paragraph at page No. 5 of her judgment not stated any reason for her award but only stated about the respective contentions of the parties as well as acquisition of property by issuing notifications.
In fact there is no specific reasons in the judgment to show the enhancement made by the respondent No.2 in her order.
In the absence of any specific reasons assigned by the respondent No. 2 for the enhancement of compensation; certainly such enhancement can not be accepted.

.17. The claim of the petitioner is that the respondent No.3 passed the award in accordance with Sections 26 to 30 as well as first schedule of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

1 to demonstrate A.P. No.32/2024 that the award passed by the LAO is not accordance with Section 26 to 30 as well as first Schedule of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

sentences.text: It is also not the grievance of the respondent No.1 in the application for enhancement of compensation that the respondent No.3 / LAO has not granted the compensation as contemplated under the aforesaid provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: There is no material on record to show that the LAO has not calculated the interest as per guidelines given in the aforesaid provision of law to determine the market value.
Under such circumstances, A.P. No.32/2024 certainly the award passed by the LAO cannot be accepted.

.19. It is also not the case of the petitioner before the LAO or Arbitrator that the respondent No.3 /
LAO has not awarded the compensation as stated in the aforesaid provision of law.

The award /
judgment passed by the Arbitrator / respondent No.2 also nowhere discloses that the LAO has not considered the parameter of the aforesaid provision of law i.e., Sections 26 to 30 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 to determine the market value.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The Gazette notification produced by the petitioner sufficiently discloses that the respondent No.3/ LAO considered the guidance value for registration of sale deeds or agreements to sell and awarded the said amount as compensation.

When the LAO has granted the compensation as per Section 26(1)(a) of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, certainly the A.P. No.32/2024 Arbitrator is estopped from enhancing the compensation.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The Arbitrator in the aforesaid judgment nowhere stated or discussed or pointed out that the Arbitrator has not followed the aforesaid provisions of law in determining the market value.
It is also not the case of the respondent No.1 before the respondent No.2 that the LAO has not passed the individual award.
Therefore, it is clear that the respondent No.3 / LAO has passed individual award by considering all the relevant facts.
Under such circumstances, certainly the award passed by the LAO cannot be set aside or modified or changed.
In view of all these facts, certainly the award passed by the Arbitrator cannot be accepted and that should be intervened by the Court.
Hence, this Court is of the humble opinion that the petitioner has made out sufficient grounds to intervene with the award passed by the Arbitrator and the award is liable to be set aside.
Accordingly, the above point is held in the affirmative.

In the result following:
A.P. No.32/2024 ORDER Petition filed under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 by the petitioner is hereby allowed.
Consequently, the award passed by the Arbitrator / respondent No.2 in case No. LAQ / ARB / NH-844 / CR / 43/ 2021- 22 and LAQ / ARB / NH-844 / CR / 42/ 2021-22 dated 26.02.2024 pertaining to Sy.
No.73/2 measuring 1620 Sq.
Meters and Survey No.73/3 measuring 655 Sq. Meters of Halehalli village is hereby set aside with a liberty to the parties to pursue their remedy in accordance with law.

1 to demonstrate A.P. No.32/2024 that the award passed by the LAO is not accordance with Section 26 to 30 as well as first Schedule of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
Even there is no reasoning in the award that the LAO had not followed the aforesaid provisions and even there is no material on record to show that the Arbitrator has gone through the award passed by the LAO and modified or enhanced the compensation.
It is also not the grievance of the respondent No.1 in the application for enhancement of compensation that the respondent No.3 / LAO has not granted the compensation as contemplated under the aforesaid provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
There is no material on record to show that the LAO has not calculated the interest as per guidelines given in the aforesaid provision of law to determine the market value.
The award /
judgment passed by the Arbitrator / respondent No.2 also nowhere discloses that the LAO has not considered the parameter of the aforesaid provision of law i.e., Sections 26 to 30 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 to determine the market value.
The Gazette notification produced by the petitioner sufficiently discloses that the respondent No.3/ LAO considered the guidance value for registration of sale deeds or agreements to sell and awarded the said amount as compensation.
When the LAO has granted the compensation as per Section 26(1)(a) of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, certainly the A.P. No.32/2024 Arbitrator is estopped from enhancing the compensation.

Accordingly, the above point is held in the affirmative.
In the result following:
A.P. No.32/2024 ORDER Petition filed under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 by the petitioner is hereby allowed.
Consequently, the award passed by the Arbitrator / respondent No.2 in case No. LAQ / ARB / NH-844 / CR / 43/ 2021- 22 and LAQ / ARB / NH-844 / CR / 42/ 2021-22 dated 26.02.2024 pertaining to Sy.
No.73/2 measuring 1620 Sq.
Meters and Survey No.73/3 measuring 655 Sq. Meters of Halehalli village is hereby set aside with a liberty to the parties to pursue their remedy in accordance with law.
Office is directed to send back the Lower Court Records.
